from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuition: From 2D to 3D", ["We start with a 2D circle.", "Transition to a 3D sphere.", "Slicing reveals inner geometry."])
        
        # 2D Object (Square used for intuition as requested)
        shape_2d = Square(color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(shape_2d, 'C2', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # 3D Object (Cube used for transition)
        shape_3d = Cube(side_length=2.0, fill_color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_at_grid(shape_3d, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Labels
        label_2d = Text("2D Area", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2d, 'D2')
        
        label_3d = Text("3D Volume", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_3d, 'D5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(shape_2d), FadeIn(label_2d))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(shape_2d.copy(), shape_3d), FadeIn(label_3d))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        slice_plane = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(slice_plane, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(slice_plane))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

        # Show distance formula/volume context
        vol_formula = MathTex(r"V_n(R) = \frac{\pi^{n/2}}{\Gamma(n/2 + 1)} R^n", color="#00CED1")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Data points become sparse.", "Distance metrics lose meaning.", "Curse of dimensionality explained."]
        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Data Science", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # Animation 1: Sparse points
        data_points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color="#00CED1") for _ in range(20)])
        for p in data_points:
            p.move_to(np.array([np.random.uniform(1.5, 5.5), np.random.uniform(-1.5, 1.5), 0]))
        
        # Animation 2: Projection
        projection_line = Line(start=np.array([1, 0, 0]), end=np.array([6, 0, 0]), color="#FF1493")
        projected_points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color="#FF1493") for _ in range(20)])
        for i, p in enumerate(data_points):
            projected_points[i].move_to(np.array([p.get_x(), 0, 0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF1493"))
        self.play(Create(projection_line), FadeIn(projected_points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Show label
        label = Text("Curse of Dimensionality", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Exploring the Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres

sections.title: Intuition: From 2D to 3D
sections.content: Establish prerequisite knowledge by visualizing the transition from a circle (2D) to a sphere (3D). Define the volume/area relationship through cross-sectional slices to build the foundation for higher dimensions.
sections.example: An apple being sliced: A 2D circle slice reveals the 'area' of the 3D fruit cross-section.

sections.title: Mathematical Generalization (N-dimensions)
sections.content: Introduce the hypersphere equation: x1² + x2² + ... + xn² = R². Explain how the volume formula V_n(R) = [π^(n/2) / Γ(n/2 + 1)] * R^n evolves as 'n' increases.
sections.example: A 'Robot Sphere' expanding its coordinate axes from x, y, z to include w, v, etc., demonstrating the formal mathematical expansion.

sections.title: The Paradox: Where is the Volume?
sections.content: Highlight the counter-intuitive phenomenon: as dimensions increase, the volume of a unit hypersphere concentrates near the surface, and eventually approaches zero as n → ∞.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Hedgehog' in 100D: All its volume is in the 'quills' (surface shell), while the 'body' (inner core) has virtually no volume.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Data Science
sections.content: Apply the concept of high-dimensional spheres to explain the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Machine Learning, where data points become increasingly sparse in high-dimensional feature spaces.
sections.example: A data-processing AI trying to find a needle in a haystack; as dimensions increase, the 'hay' (space) expands so rapidly that the 'needle' (data point) becomes impossible to locate.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the progression from visual geometry to abstract algebra. Final takeaway: Higher dimensions are not just 'more space,' but fundamentally different geometric environments.
sections.example: A final graphic showing a sphere transitioning from a solid object to a 'ghostly' frame as it passes through the 4th dimension.
